text: Under the Employment Insurance Act, a claimant must serve a waiting period of two weeks before becoming entitled to benefits.
Under the Employment Insurance Act, an insured person must have had an interruption of earnings from employment in order to qualify for benefits.
The number of insurable hours required to qualify for Employment Insurance benefits is the same across all regions of Canada.
Under the Employment Insurance Act, parental benefits may be paid to care for a child placed for adoption.
A claimant who has accumulated violations under the Employment Insurance Act may be required to accumulate more insurable hours to qualify for benefits.
Employment Insurance benefits may be paid to a claimant who remains fully employed.
The Employment Insurance Act defines a claimant as a person who applies or has applied for benefits under the Act.
Under the Employment Insurance Act, parental benefits can only be received by one parent per child.
